newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mongolia becomes new member of world trade body.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia becomes new member of world trade body.

text.p: Ex-communist Mongolia became the first transition economy of the old Soviet bloc to join the World Trade Organisation as a new member on Wednesday.
Officials at the world trade body said the Asian state's entry brought to 130 the number of WTO members.

Many former communist states in eastern and central Europe, as well as Cuba, were long members of the old General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and became founder members of the WTO when it was launched in January 1995.
Like the old Soviet Union, Mongolia -- a remote country wedged between China and Russia -- for decades regarded the GATT as "an instrument of exploitation" by the West of developing countries.

Elections last year won by a reformist democratic coalition ended more than 75 years of rule by communists and their heirs. The new government has promised economic reforms and privatisation and is courting foreign investors.
Mongolia applied to join GATT in 1991.
Neither Russia nor China -- whose long-standing bid has been delayed by United States and Western European insistence that it provide more access to its markets -- are yet members of WTO.

Of the 15 republics of the former communist empire, 11 have also applied -- Armenia, Belarus, Estonia, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova, Ukraine, Uzbekistan and Georgia, which became an observer earlier in 1996.
